title: Every length follows Settings ▸ Units
rule: Every length a person reads or types (field, label, tooltip, menu, report, CSV, web page, voice) is in the unit chosen in Settings ▸ Units, feet and inches by default.
why: 2026-11-06: Set Mounting Height… asked "Height above the floor (metres):" on a feet show, after the same field was fixed on 2026-10-27 (Q174). About 55 call sites keyed off the grid unit; he: "we keep finding places where it exists".

example.right: Height above the floor: 12' 6"
example.wrong: Height above the floor (metres): 3.81

patterns.when: Settings ▸ Units = feet and inches (the default)

title: A length field is a length field
rule: A length is typed into a LengthSpinBox or MeasurementEdit (LengthInputDialog for a prompt) that takes any unit, never a bare number box.
why: 2026-11-06: the Mounting Height prompt was a QInputDialog::getDouble labelled in metres; a number box can't say its unit or take 12' 6".

example.right: A Trim field that takes 18' 0", 18ft or 5.5 m and shows 18' 0"
example.wrong: QInputDialog::getDouble(this, tr("Trim"), tr("Height (m)"), ...)

title: The grid's unit is only for the grid
rule: The show grid's unit sets grid spacing only; nothing picks a display unit from it.
why: 2026-11-06: the root cause of the metres-on-a-feet-show class of bugs was MonitorProperties::gridUnits() used to choose the display unit.

example.right: MeasurementUnits::formatLength(mm) in a label
example.wrong: gridUnits() == Meters ? "%1 m" : "%1 ft"

title: Feet and inches read like a tape measure
rule: Imperial lengths show feet and inches to the nearest 1/8", the fraction reduced, and the same forms are accepted when typed.
why: 2026-11-06 (5eb8b86c7): decimals of a foot are not how a crew measures or calls a trim.

title: Values in the user's terms
rule: A setting shows its meaning, not its storage: an option's name, a switch's sense, "per beat" on a speed master, one cycle's seconds for a wave, lengths through Units.
why: 2026-11-06 (b3784b1b6): an effect in the tree showed raw script parameters; the effect rows now read like the Aim row.

example.right: Direction: Reverse · Speed: 2 per beat
example.wrong: direction: 1 · speed: 0.5

title: A typed value stays when you click away
rule: A typed fade, hold or value is committed when focus leaves the field, not only on Return.
why: 2026-10-23 (Q60, quick win 2/14): typed times were lost on a click into the tree.

example.right: Type 2.5 in Fade, click the tree: Fade is 2.5
example.wrong: Type 2.5 in Fade, click the tree: Fade is back to 0

title: Help gives a length in feet first, metric in brackets
rule: A help page writes a length in feet and inches with the metric after it in brackets, 4 ft (1.2 m); never a metric length on its own.
why: 2026-11-07: the Wand help said "1.2 m", "2 cm" and "25 mm" on a product whose lengths default to feet; it now reads "4 ft (1.2 m)" (feat/042-wand-spacing). Help can't follow the setting, so it gives both, feet first (UX-01).

example.right: Wand length: the staff, 4 ft (1.2 m) unless set.
example.wrong: Wand length: the staff, 1.2 m unless set.

title: Menu items are Title Case
rule: Every menu item is Title Case: every word capitalised except a, an, the, and, or, of, to, in, on, at, by, for, from, with, as, vs, into after the first.
why: 2026-11-02/03 menu canon (docs/design/CONTEXT_MENUS.md §3.2): the same action was worded three ways in three menus.

example.right: Delete Fixture Group…
example.wrong: Delete fixture group…

title: Buttons are Title Case too
rule: Every push or tool button text is Title Case like a menu item (dialog-box answers such as "Not now" excepted).
why: 2026-11-06: "Show all effects" on the effect picker; train 1106b failed on it.

example.right: Show All Effects
example.wrong: Show all effects

title: "…" means a dialog follows
rule: A label ends in the single character "…" exactly when a dialog (including a confirmation) follows; never three dots; an inline rename has none.

example.right: Patch…  ·  Rename (inline)
example.wrong: Patch...  ·  Rename… (inline)

title: No shortcut typed into a label
rule: A shortcut is set on the action so Qt shows it in its own column; it is never part of the text.

example.right: Select All     ⌘A
example.wrong: Select All (Ctrl+A)

title: Delete destroys, Remove takes out
rule: "Delete X…" destroys the thing; "Remove from Y" takes it out of a container and leaves it in the show. A bare "Remove" is never a destroy.
why: 2026-11-02 menu canon §3.2: "Remove" meant both in different menus.

example.right: Remove from Truss  ·  Delete Fixture Group…
example.wrong: Remove (an item that deletes the fixture group)

title: One word per idea
rule: Each idea has one name everywhere: Hits (the busk section), Plot symbol, Operate, Hold at end, Quick Focus / Venue Focus / Focus This Cue.
why: 2026-10-23 (Q70, Q77) and 2026-10-25 (Q149): "look", "focus" and "stage look" each meant several things.

example.right: Plot symbol · Hits · Focus This Cue
example.wrong: Stage Look · Looks (the busk section) · Refine

title: Release and Untrack
rule: Ending a tracked layer is Release (plays in this cue, then lets go) or Untrack (never reaches this cue), the same words in menus, tooltips, the tracking column, help, course, command line and voice.
why: 2026-11-04 (Q222): he turned off the USTs' tracking and expected them gone from the cue he was on; the words had to say which.

example.right: Release After This Cue  ·  Untrack From This Cue
example.wrong: Drop From This Cue  ·  Stop Tracking  ·  Block

title: "Classic" means stock QLC+
rule: Anything labelled Classic is stock QLC+ 4 only; qlcconsole's own tools never wear the word.
why: 2026-10-23 (Q73): "Build ▸ Scenes ▸ Classic" was not QLC+'s.

example.right: View ▸ Workspace ▸ Classic QLC+ (the stock tabs and toolbars)
example.wrong: Build ▸ Scenes ▸ Classic

title: A jump names where it goes
rule: A link, Go to or Open item names its destination in the user's terms.
why: 2026-11-06 (b7cee01ad): a grey row's "Go to" didn't say which cue.

example.right: Go to 1.1.1 Setup
example.wrong: Go to origin

title: Keys and buttons are named as on the device in hand
rule: Shortcuts read ⌘/⌥/⇧ on macOS and Ctrl/Alt/Shift elsewhere; a game pad's buttons are named as printed on that pad (Cross, Circle, Options on PlayStation; A, B, Menu on Xbox), in text and voice.
why: 2026-10-27 (Q170): about 45 hard-coded Xbox strings told a DualShock user to press A. 2026-10-15 (270e59ecc): help on Windows told people to press ⌘.

example.right: ⌘D on a Mac · "Press ✕ to keep" on a DualSense
example.wrong: Ctrl+D in the Mac help · "Press A to keep" on a DualSense

title: Plain sentences, not engine terms
rule: Explanations, warnings and errors say what happened in the operator's words and what to do next; engine terms (HTP, fader priority, function id) stay out.
why: 2026-10-27 (Q181, Why is this on?) and the teaching shows: the answer has to be readable by a student on headset.

example.right: Par 3 is at 80% because cue 2.1 Verse sets it.
example.wrong: Channel 37: HTP, fader priority Override, function #112

title: Cue numbers and names follow his scheme
rule: Cue numbers are {S}.{P}.{II}, period separated, any level past 9; scene names follow SS-PP.II-Description, learned from siblings when duplicating.
why: 2026-10-29 (Q190 and his stated scheme): song sections are derived from the number, so the format has to hold.

example.wrong: 1.A · 1.9 renumbered to 2.0 · "Chorus Wash copy"

title: QLC+ 4.x is in maintenance
rule: Text about upstream says QLC+ 4.x is in maintenance; never abandoned or dead.
why: 2026-10-28 strategy (Q186): qlcconsole is a home for 4.x users, not a campaign against upstream.

example.right: QLC+ 4.x is in maintenance upstream.
example.wrong: QLC+ 4 is abandoned.

title: Lists fit the fixtures in play
rule: A picker or list offers what fits the fixtures it will act on, with a Title Case "Show All …" to see the rest, and never drops the item already in use.
why: 2026-11-06: effect search offered WLED effects for groups with no WLED device. 2026-11-06 (e1c558d12): the fitted effect picker had to keep a look's current effect even when it no longer fit.

example.right: Pars selected: colour and dimmer effects, [Show All Effects]
example.wrong: Pars selected: "WLED: Fireworks" at the top of the list

title: Plain words just work
rule: The command line takes commands and plain language in the same box; it decides typo vs language itself and never needs "?" or a prefix.
why: 2026-11-06: the command line made him type "?" to reach AI Assist.

example.right: "make the towers blue" goes to AI Assist; "dimer 50" offers Did you mean dimmer 50
example.wrong: Unknown command. Type ? to ask AI.

title: Show what it acts on and where each value comes from
rule: A row for an effect, palette or layer shows what it runs on (and, on a mixed target, how much of it and why not the rest) and, for each value, its origin: own, from a palette or preset, script default, tracked from a cue. Like an Aim row.
why: 2026-11-06: an effect in the Show Tree didn't show its group or its values. 2026-11-06 (b3784b1b6): a position effect on towers of movers and pars silently ran on half.

example.right: Runs on: Towers (2 of 4 fixtures: Pars have no pan/tilt) · Speed 2 per beat, from Effect “Chase”
example.wrong: EFX 3 (no target, no values)

title: Nothing to say, nothing shown
rule: A chip, button or column with nothing to report stays hidden until it has something: power without sources, MTC without a source, Upgrade without chasers, Productions with one production.
why: 2026-10-23 (Q75, Q89, Q90, Q98): the footer and headers were full of "MTC: no source" and empty controls.

example.right: No MTC chip until a timecode source is set
example.wrong: MTC: no source (in every show's footer)

title: F1 opens help on what's in front
rule: Every dialog and view carries a helpTopic, so F1 opens the guide for it.
why: 2026-10-10 in-app help: context-aware help was the ask; a new dialog without a topic drops to Getting Started.

example.right: F1 in Venue Focus opens focus-calls.md
example.wrong: F1 in a new dialog opens getting-started.md

patterns.require: every top-level QDialog has a non-empty helpTopic property

title: A console setting holds on every surface
rule: A choice made on the console (feedback mode, units, view) is what the pad, voice, web page and dialogs use, without asking again.
why: 2026-10-24 (Q127): "this should default to what's set on the console and follow that thru the entire operation."

example.right: Feedback: Lights on the console; the pad gives lights, no voice
example.wrong: The pad starts in Lights + Voice whatever the console says

title: Anything that waits shows it is busy
rule: An action that can take more than a moment shows a busy sign where it was asked, what it is waiting on, how to cancel, and elapsed seconds after 2 s.
why: 2026-11-06: no sign AI Assist was working.

example.right: ⟳ Asking AI Assist (llama3)… 4 s · Esc cancels
example.wrong: The line just sits there

title: A greyed control says why
rule: Every disabled button or menu item says on hover why, and how to make it available when there is a way.
why: 2026-10-25 (Q146): Focus mode's Start was greyed with no reason; 2026-10-23 (Q81): Undo silently did nothing.

example.right: Start (greyed) — "Needs a moving head and a stage target"
example.wrong: Start (greyed), no tooltip

patterns.require: every visible disabled QAbstractButton/QAction has a non-empty toolTip or statusTip

title: Nothing is refused silently
rule: When the app won't do something, it says what and why where the person is looking; a drop of something compatible does what it obviously means instead of refusing (a group set on a scene adds its member groups).
why: 2026-11-03 (Q205): Add Fixture past universe 1024 silently added nothing. 2026-10-23 (Q86): a group set dropped on a Build scene was refused with no word.

example.right: "Universe 1025 is past the limit (1024). Nothing was added."
example.wrong: Dialog closes, no fixture

title: Red is for real problems
rule: Red means something is wrong on a real rig; "not set up yet" or "nothing patched" is neutral grey.
why: 2026-10-23 (Q64): a new show with no outputs said red Not ready.

example.right: grey "No outputs: preview only"
example.wrong: red "Not ready" on an empty show

title: Prompts are quiet lines, once
rule: A suggestion goes in the notice bar with a button, once per session; a modal dialog is only for a destructive or blocking choice.
why: 2026-10-23 (Q92): GO in Design offers Operate in the notice bar, not a dialog.

example.right: Notice bar: You're in Design. Switch to Operate? [Switch]
example.wrong: A modal box on every GO

title: One edit, one undo; ⌘Z says where it doesn't work
rule: Every user action is one undo step (however many objects it touches), and where ⌘Z doesn't work Edit ▸ Undo is greyed with "Nothing to undo on this tab".
why: 2026-10-23 (Q81) and 2026-10-24 (Q117): ⌘Z silently did nothing on some tabs, and one Keep took two undos.

example.right: Dragging a cue-list clip 6 s later: one Undo puts every cue back
example.wrong: Undo restores half the cues; ⌘Z on Run does nothing, silently

title: Warnings keep their state visible
rule: A warning is open (amber), meant (green, with who, when and note on hover) or not applicable (listed in Show Review under Accepted); answered warnings don't vanish.
why: 2026-11-03 (Q210): answered cyc warnings disappeared from the cue.

example.right: cyc ✓ (hover: Branson, 11-03, intended wash)
example.wrong: the warning gone with no trace

title: The footer tells the state of the rig
rule: The footer always shows what the stage is showing (LIVE, Blind, Build look, holds), the venue, and one chip listing everything overriding the rig (Park, Highlight, Flash, Solo, Focus, Blind, Hold at end) that clears them with a click.
why: 2026-10-24 (Q129) venue chip; 2026-11-03 (b7d0d24cb) stage chip: he couldn't tell what was on the output. 2026-10-23 (Q80): overrides were spread across several indicators.

example.right: LIVE 2.1 Verse · Venue: Lincoln HS · Overrides: Park 2, Solo ▸ Clear All
example.wrong: Blind on with nothing in the footer; a Park light here, a Solo badge there

title: No overlap or clipping at three sizes
rule: Every screen, editor and dialog lays out without overlapping or clipped widgets at 1024×640, 1280×800 and 1920×1080, and the tab strip fits the window with no scroll arrows.
why: 2026-11-03 (Q207): the colour picker's "Wheel / ring" row lay under other widgets. 2026-11-04 (3fa7b2d9e): tabs scrolled off a laptop screen.

example.right: every row readable at 1024×640
example.wrong: a row drawn under the one below it

title: Footer items share one line
rule: The footer's right-side items sit on one line, centred, at equal height and padding, and never overlap.
why: 2026-11-04 (d8a0acac0) and again 2026-11-06: footer chips misaligned.

example.right: GM · Ready · Venue chips on one baseline
example.wrong: one chip 3 px lower and taller than its neighbours

title: Words people must read are never cut
rule: State text, cue names and anything a lesson tells students to read is shown whole at the smallest window size.
why: 2026-10-24 (Q115): the Run tab cut "▷ STANDBY" to "▷ STA…" though lesson 1.5 says to read it.

example.right: ▷ STANDBY
example.wrong: ▷ STA…

patterns.require: no elided text in state columns, chips or buttons

title: Readable in every theme
rule: Text, state colours and cue colours stay readable in every theme (Default, Blue, Red Shift, QLC+ Original, dark).
why: 2026-10-15 (270e59ecc) Windows themes and 2026-10-22 cue colours: text vanished on some themes.

example.right: a yellow cue colour drawn darker on a light theme so it reads
example.wrong: yellow cue text on a white row

title: Panels open inside the main window
rule: Pickers and helper panels dock in the main window or open in front of it; nothing opens behind it.
why: 2026-10-23 (Q61): pickers opened behind the main window.

example.right: the colour picker docks beside the Look Editor
example.wrong: the picker opens behind the main window

patterns.require: every new top-level window is a child of the main window and is raised

title: Plot overlays line up
rule: Rulers, readouts, handles and selection rings on the plot sit on the thing they mark at every zoom and view.
why: 2026-10-27 (Q179): 13 of 27 Lighting Studio overlays were off.

example.right: a target's readout under the target at 4× zoom
example.wrong: the readout a fixture-width off at 4×

title: A UI change shows its before and after
rule: A change to ui/, web pages or the rig view ships with before/after shots at 1024×640, 1280×800 and 1920×1080 that he reviews before merge.
why: 2026-11-03 (Q207): "do we not do after-patch checking to see that the result matches intended behavior?"

example.right: shots-041/<agent>/before-1280x800.png, after-1280x800.png ...
example.wrong: "gate=0" as the only evidence for a layout change

title: One object, one menu
rule: Right-clicking an object anywhere gives the place's own items on top, one separator, then the same kind block in the fixed order Open, Kind, Selection, Organise, Edit, Remove.
why: 2026-11-03: "a line on rig view or in tree .. should still have the same paradigm where the right click can edit all the things that I can in the build".

example.right: Set to ▸ · None (off here) | Edit Palette · ... · Delete Palette…
example.wrong: Delete in the middle; a different palette menu in the Show Tree

title: Duplicate means one thing and works on everything
rule: ⌘D is Duplicate in every list, no two application shortcuts share a key, and every kind of list item (cue, layer, hit, cue list, production, reusable cue, palette, truss, target) offers Duplicate, Copy and Paste.
why: 2026-11-04 (Q214): ⌘D meant Duplicate, Dump DMX and Delete Universe in three places. 2026-11-04 (Q215): a festival cut of a cue list meant rebuilding it.

example.right: ⌘D duplicates the selected universe's row; ⌫ deletes it
example.wrong: ⌘D deletes a universe on Connections

title: One selection everywhere
rule: The plot, Workbench, Fixtures, Flash/Park/Highlight and the pad act on one selection, like an Eos magic sheet.
why: 2026-11-02 (Q201): each view kept its own selection.

example.right: select SL towers on the plot; the Workbench shows them selected
example.wrong: the Workbench still shows the previous pick

title: Surface area stays flat
rule: A new menu item, tab, panel or mode replaces one or is justified in writing; the menu-item count is flat or falling each release; a new top-level tab or playback path needs his explicit yes.
why: 2026-10-23 review (102-item menus, 8+ tabs), freeze Q82; 2026-11-02 (Q200): two new entries folded.

example.right: Calling Script… folded under More ▾
example.wrong: a new top-level "Tools" menu

title: One GO path
rule: Every GO (keys, Run tab, VC Cue Runner, pad, OSC, web) ends in the same call with its route, so they behave the same.
why: 2026-10-23 (Q74), built 2026-10-31: GO did slightly different things from different places.

example.right: pad GO and Space both fire App::runCommand()
example.wrong: a VC button that steps the chaser directly

title: Solo and Play on every cue and layer page
rule: Solo and Play are available on every cue and layer page, docked or not (greyed with a reason in Operate).
why: 2026-11-01: "the solo in layer is working great .. that's a huge plus"; Solo had silently gone missing from one page.

example.right: Solo on the docked Workbench's layer row
example.wrong: Solo only on the undocked page

title: Positions relative to the stage
rule: Where a light points is expressed against stage targets and lines (Aim, Formation) before raw pan/tilt.
why: 2026-11-01: "tying the layout to the targets .. that's gonna help a lot"; Q197/Q206 split Aim (where) from Formation (how they spread).

example.right: Aim: DSC · Formation: pairs, crossed
example.wrong: Pan 127 / Tilt 64 typed per fixture

title: QLC+ habits stay first-class
rule: A QLC+ 4 show opens as it was and sends the same DMX; nothing nags or converts on load; upgrading is one menu item when asked.
why: 2026-10-22 (Q29) and 2026-10-23 (Q63, Q76): never nag, never convert on load.

example.right: a 4.x show opens in Classic QLC+, shutters as saved
example.wrong: "Convert this show now?" on open

title: Operate refuses edits from every input
rule: In Operate, edits are refused from menus, the command line, AI Assist, the web page and the pad alike, each with a line saying so.
why: 2026-11-03 (Q202): typed effect fades still worked in Operate.

example.right: "effect fade 2" in Operate: "Edits are off in Operate."
example.wrong: the fade changes during the show

title: Esc is not a stop
rule: Plain Esc never stops playback; Stop All is ⌘⇧Esc.
why: 2026-10-25 (c8f278d0b): Esc to close a panel stopped the running list.

example.right: Esc closes the picker; the cue keeps running
example.wrong: Esc closes the picker and blacks the stage

title: Focusing during a show is quiet
rule: Focusing in Operate shows nothing to the audience: no blink or dim, only the running cue, and the hold lets go on GO.
why: 2026-10-24 (Q130): Refine in Operate blinked and dimmed lights live.

example.right: a touch-up on cue 3 changes only that light, smoothly
example.wrong: every other light dims to 15% mid-song

title: A hold never confirms a warning
rule: Holding a pad button may act, but never answers a warning or confirmation; that takes a deliberate press.
why: 2026-10-24 (Q132): a held A could confirm the shared-palette warning and change every scene.

example.right: hold A (1.0 s) saves; the shared-palette warning still waits for a press
example.wrong: hold A saves and confirms the warning in one go

title: Safety lines always speak
rule: A controller dropping out or coming back is announced, and warnings, refusals, "controller lost" and the venue ask are spoken even when feedback is Lights only, with a distinct rumble/light pattern.
why: 2026-10-24 (Q131): in Lights only a Start on stage got no answer. 2026-10-24 (88409a2a7, Q131): a pad going to sleep froze the session with no word.

example.right: Lights only: "Controller lost" is still said
example.wrong: Lights only: silence when the pad drops

title: Remote GO is off until the show allows it
rule: A GO from the phone or web page is refused until Show Settings allow remote GO, and the Operate PIN still applies.

example.right: web GO: "Remote GO is off for this show"
example.wrong: anyone on the Wi-Fi can GO

title: A locked plot moves nothing
rule: With the plot locked, nothing moves or drops, targets included, unless "Targets stay adjustable" is on.
why: 2026-10-27 (Q183): a locked platform still saved where it was dropped.

example.right: drag on a locked plot: nothing moves, the lock flashes
example.wrong: the truss snaps to where it was dropped on release

title: Fixed means checked on his real path
rule: A fix for something he hit on his rig is "fixed" only after it is checked on his show, patch and device layer; otherwise the report says exactly what was and wasn't checked.
why: 2026-11-04: the follow spot was reported fixed three times on faked input; "DO NOT REPORT FIXED UNTIL YOU HAVE VALIDATED THAT WORKS".

example.right: "HID plugin on dink, DanceHysteria-0.6, stick moved the spot: PASS"
example.wrong: "fixed (unit test injects stick values)"

title: Students are crew
rule: Student text uses real theatre vocabulary defined once, normal sentence rhythm, and no kid-speak, cheerleading, reassurance or talk about style.
why: 2026-10-21: the course's talk about tone and short sentences was "a bit condescending".

example.right: "A cue that tracks keeps its levels until a later cue changes them."
example.wrong: "Great job! Don't worry, tracking is easy!"

patterns.forbid_regex: (?i)\b(great job|awesome|don't worry|no worries|you've got this|short sentences|super easy)\b|!{2,}

title: Why first, one idea per step
rule: Every lesson, app lessons included, opens with why it matters; then one idea per step, splitting a long lesson rather than cutting a fundamental.
why: 2026-10-29: "they need to know the WHY of what they're doing before the HOW." 2026-10-28: "the course should be simple and concise" (handouts ran ~1,600 words).

example.right: "Tracking saves re-setting every light each cue." then 3. Select the towers. 4. Press Aim.
example.wrong: "Step 1: click + Cue, select the towers, press Aim, choose DSC and save."

title: One student link per lesson, no teacher material
rule: A student gets one link per lesson that holds everything for it and leads nowhere near teacher guides or answer keys.
why: 2026-10-28 and 2026-10-29 (Q187): the course site showed answer keys to everyone.

example.right: sandinak.github.io/qlcconsole/class/1-1/
example.wrong: a lesson page linking to TEACHER.md

title: Help ships with the feature
rule: A feature lands with its help page (and a course note where it applies); every help link resolves, no bare <tag> eats a page, and screenshots are retaken after a UI change (tools/help-shots.sh, Blue theme) with callouts that match the key.
why: 2026-10-10 in-app help; 2026-10-28 strategy guardrail 2: no "help later". 2026-10-23 (Q72): pictures still showed "Programming" and a clipped Look Editor.

example.right: "WLED: <effect>" in the guide
example.wrong: "WLED: <effect>" (the rest of the page disappears)

title: Findable from where you work
rule: A feature is reachable, or pointed to, from the place a person does that work: its control, or one line naming where it is, is on that screen.
why: 2026-11-07: he looked for song sections on the cue list (right-click a cue, the list's page); they are switched on only by Numbering on the production's page, and nothing on the list pointed there. The hint on the list page is on feat/042-section-hint.

example.right: The list's page: "Sections follow the production's Numbering (None)." with a link to it
example.wrong: The list's page with no word of sections; Numbering only on the production's page

title: Testable where it's built
rule: Anything you build can be tried from where you build it, in Design, without switching to Operate.
why: 2026-11-07: he needed to test a hit's key while programming, and keys fired only in Operate; they now fire in Design when the hit is armed (the Run tab's list, or selected in the Show Tree), on feat/042-key-triggers.

example.right: A hit selected in the Show Tree, Design: F7 plays it
example.wrong: F7 does nothing until Operate

title: Read it from the device
rule: Configuration a device already holds is read from it, not typed in by hand; typing stays as the fallback.
why: 2026-11-07: a WLED fountain's sprinkle-loop spans could only be typed into a table; Read Segments now imports them from the device and Edit Spans… stays for changes (feat/042-fountain-sprinkles). "Don't make him count what the device knows."

example.right: Spans: [Read Segments] (6 spans from the WLED) · Edit Spans…
example.wrong: Spans: type First LED and Last LED for each of 6 spans

title: Auto is right for the real gear and shows its number
rule: An Auto setting works its value out from the gear as it is set up, and shows the number it chose.
why: 2026-11-07: a wand's Auto turns assumed LED tape and drew half a turn for a 16 ft fairy string; Auto now works from the string's length and shows "Auto (58.5)" (feat/042-wand-spacing).

example.right: Turns: Auto (58.5)
example.wrong: Turns: Auto  (half a turn drawn on a 16 ft string)

title: Easy to find, quick to use
rule: A student finds a core task from where they are working without being told, and a professional isn't slowed down doing it.
why: 2026-11-07, approving the flows: "this tool will be used by students and professionals .. it needs some level of ease of use while being somewhat comprehensive .. if I have to explain everything all the time, even with training, then we've failed in the design." The checks are under Complexity and ease of use; the flows under Flows.

example.right: Number a show into songs: 5 clicks, each control on the screen before it
example.wrong: A core flow whose next control is found only in the help

title: A device you add is reachable
rule: Adding a network fixture leaves it on an output that reaches it; one that can't be reached says so in the footer, with a one-click fix.
why: 2026-11-07: he added a WLED (Connection: Network (WLED), IP 172.18.2.100) through Add Fixture. It landed on universe 1, whose output is Art-Net to his node, so nothing reached the WLED; moving it by hand to universe 2 left that universe with no output at all (fix/042-wled-add-patch).

example.right: Add Fixture (WLED) → its own universe, WLED output, sent to its IP
example.wrong: WLED on U01-Office (Art-Net to 172.18.2.10), no warning

title: A control shown works on that fixture, or says why not
rule: A control is offered only where it does something for that fixture; where it can't, it is greyed with the reason (UX-27).
why: 2026-11-07: Runs (Once / N times) and At the end (Hold / Release) were offered for a WLED device effect and did nothing. "When I set it to once .. it does the entire thing once .. and then does it again"; "hold and release don't appear to do much" (fix/042-wled-runs).

example.right: Runs: Once on a WLED effect → it plays once, then holds
example.wrong: Runs: Once offered on a WLED effect; it loops anyway

title: A copy is a copy
rule: Duplicate, Copy and Paste never leave a hidden link; anything still shared says where else it is used and offers Own Copy.
why: 2026-11-07: duplicating a cue shared the layer's own (inline) looks, so "all the edits to the layer go to both cues", and the Look Editor showed no "Used by" for them (fix/042-duplicate-own-looks).

example.right: Duplicate a cue, change the copy's colour: the original keeps its colour
example.wrong: Duplicate a cue, change the copy: both cues change, and the Look Editor says nothing is shared

title: A cue shows what it asks for
rule: Nothing carries in from earlier cues except tracked values, and what tracks is visible; a cue's look is what it says.
why: 2026-11-07, his words: "unless tracked .. new cue should apply all new values to meet the required look". A colour-only cue after a Fireworks Starburst cue left the WLED still running Starburst: its effect setting latched, because non-intensity channels keep their last value (fix/042-wled-runs).

example.right: A colour-only cue after Starburst: the WLED goes to solid colour
example.wrong: A colour-only cue after Starburst: the WLED keeps running Starburst

title: Properties fit the kind of device
rule: A fixture's properties show what that kind of device has: a pixel string shows string things (connection, IP, LED count, length, pixel path), not a mounted light's.
why: 2026-11-07: Fixture Properties showed a WLED fairy string as a mounted light (orientation, pan/tilt, beam). "Not sure that is how that should work for strings connected to it (we may do other things in the future that utilize this idea .. but not yet)" (fix/042-wled-add-patch).

example.right: WLED string: Connection, IP, LED count, String length, Pixel path
example.wrong: WLED string: Orientation, Pan/Tilt, Beam angle

title: Locate works on every patched fixture
rule: Locate is unmistakable on the device (solid, full, white, sharp flashes) over whatever is playing, and everything is back after.
why: 2026-11-07: "locate doesn't appear to work" on a WLED (fix/042-wled-locate). Then the walker (F-11): Locate from the Show Tree's right-click went to the Lighting Studio tab, which stopped the Show Tree's preview, so the cue being built (a held Starburst in amber) went dark under the flashes and never came back. Fixed (fix/042-f11-locate-tracking): Locate flashes from where it was asked.

example.right: Locate on a WLED mid-effect: solid white flashes, then the effect resumes
example.wrong: Locate on a WLED: nothing visible, the effect keeps running

title: Snap means snap on every connection
rule: A network device follows a snap within the network's own time: it is sent at once with no glide; fades use the cue's time.
why: 2026-11-07, measured on ender: a WLED over its JSON API reacts about 150 to 340 ms after DMX fixtures on a snap cue (a 100 ms send tick, about 50 ms Wi-Fi with a max of 140, and a 100 ms glide). His spell cue snaps the stage to black with the staff (a WLED) still on. Fixed (feat/042-wled-snap): a change goes at once, a step with no glide, and Move in Black presets a dark WLED's next effect so the GO is its brightness alone; on the office WLED the POST now leaves 23 ms after the Art-Net bytes reach the Pi (was 62 to 105) and the WLED has it 61 ms after (was 129, max 264).

example.right: A snap cue: the WLED changes with the DMX fixtures, within the Wi-Fi's own delay
example.wrong: A snap cue: the WLED glides in 100 ms after the others, so the staff stays on

title: Status doesn't flash
rule: A save or a routine update changes a footer chip at most once, never on and off.
why: 2026-11-07: "when I save sometimes the power and current cue in the bottom flash hard" (fix/042-footer-save-flash).

example.right: Save: the power and cue chips stay steady, or change once
example.wrong: Save: the power and cue chips blink off and on

title: Tested through the path the person uses
rule: An end-to-end test drives the same dialogs and menus the person uses, not the engine call under them. (A rule for reviewing tests.)
why: 2026-11-07: the WLED end-to-end test called the patch planner directly, so it passed while the real Add Fixture path put the WLED on an Art-Net universe (UX-67). It also bears on UX-56.

example.right: A test that opens Add Fixture, picks the WLED and the connection, and clicks OK
example.wrong: A test that calls the patch planner and checks its result

title: Keep it simple for the operator (KISS)
rule: Where a change can make the operator's job simpler, that counts for it: it raises the change, and a feature is weighed by how much it saves the person running the desk.
why: 2026-11-07, on WLEDs found on the network and patched with one right-click instead of typing an IP and counting channels: "lets add that to our rules .. KISS ... Keep It Simple Stupid .. where we can make it easier for the operator that should raise the consideration of the change or feature."

example.right: A WLED on the network shows in the Inventory: right-click ▸ Patch, done
example.wrong: Add Fixture, pick the model, type the IP, count the LEDs, then patch a universe to it
